logline: A true-crime docuseries unpacking four real neighborhoods where ordinary disputes curdled into harassment, arson, and violence, and the systems that failed to stop it in time.

pull_quotes.text: I didn't anticipate that I would watch these episodes one after the other, but I did because I couldn't stop.

seasons.review_body: Blumhouse's true-crime anthology turns from roommates to neighbors for this four-episode spinoff of Worst Roommate Ever, tracking real disputes that escalated from petty grievances into arson, harassment campaigns, and a house-levelling explosion. The series dropped July 1, 2026, too recently for Rotten Tomatoes or Metacritic to post an aggregate score. Ready Steady Cut's Naomi Mairs binged all four episodes in one sitting, writing that she did not expect to watch them back to back but could not stop, and calling the cases utterly heartbreaking evidence of systems that failed the families involved. Each episode functions as a closed, self-contained nightmare rather than a serialized mystery, the Blumhouse formula applied efficiently rather than reinvented. It is too early in the show's life to call a verdict against the rest of the franchise.
